explanation:
The /members/lookup endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection. User-controlled 'email' value is directly concatenated into a SQL query string inside an f-string and executed via SQLite's execute method. No prepared statements or escaping are used, and only lowercase conversion is applied, which does not prevent injection. An attacker can craft a payload such as "' or '1'='1" (URL-encoded) to bypass the email check and retrieve all members, or use UNION SELECT to extract data from other tables if present, making this a remotely exploitable vulnerability. PoC: GET /members/lookup?email=%27%20or%20%271%27%3d%271 HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-app.example.com

The application reflects the 'name' query parameter directly in the page title without any escaping or validation, creating a reflected Cross‑Site Scripting vulnerability. An attacker can supply malicious HTML/JavaScript in the 'name' value and it will be rendered in the <h1> tag, executing in the victim's browser. PoC: GET /dashboard?name=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C%2Fscript%3E&unread=5 HTTP/1.1\nHost: vulnerable-site.example

The application deserializes user‑controlled data from the 'cart' cookie using pickle.loads without any integrity checks. Because pickle can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, an attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that runs OS commands (e.g., os.system('id')). By base64‑url‑encoding the payload and sending it as the cart cookie, the server will deserialize and execute the attacker‑controlled code, achieving remote code execution on the server process. PoC: Generate a malicious pickle and base64‑url‑encode it, then send it in the Cookie header. Example Python to create the payload: import pickle,base64,os;class RCE:    def __reduce__(self):        return (os.system,('id',));payload=base64.urlsafe_b64encode(pickle.dumps(RCE())).decode();print(payload). Use the printed string as the value of the 'cart' cookie and request GET /cart/total. The server will deserialize the payload and execute the 'id' command, demonstrating RCE.

The endpoint exposes an IDOR vulnerability: the 'name' query parameter directly maps to a file path in REPORT_DIR and is returned to the caller without verifying the caller's rights. Because there is no authentication or authorization logic, an attacker can enumerate and retrieve any .txt or .env file in the report directory (and potentially traverse out of it). This allows unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information such as configuration files. Confidence is high as the full request‑to‑response flow is present. PoC: GET /reports/download?name=app.env HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.example.com

 (Assuming REPORT_DIR contains app.env)

The download_report handler is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion via path traversal. The only filter is a suffix check for .txt or .env, which can be satisfied with a traversal payload like ../secret.txt. The resulting path points outside REPORT_DIR, allowing an attacker to read arbitrary readable .txt/.env files on the server. PoC: GET /reports/download?name=../secret.txt HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.example.com

 (Assuming /srv/app/secret.txt exists and contains sensitive data)

The DELETE /admin/users/<user_id> endpoint allows unauthenticated callers to delete any user record by supplying the user_id path parameter. No login_required or role check is performed, so an attacker can perform an IDOR to remove or enumerate users. This is a remotely exploitable Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability. PoC: curl -X DELETE http://target.example.com/admin/users/u2

The get_invoice endpoint authenticates the request but does not verify that the authenticated user is the owner of the requested invoice. Consequently, an attacker who can obtain a valid session cookie can enumerate or retrieve other users' invoices simply by changing the invoice_id in the URL, resulting in an IDOR vulnerability. PoC: # Assume the attacker has a valid session cookie stored in cookies.txt
curl -b cookies.txt https://victim.com/invoices/101  # Retrieves Ana's invoice
curl -b cookies.txt https://victim.com/invoices/102  # Retrieves Raj's invoice

The /preview endpoint is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery. The only validation performed is a scheme check for http:// or https://, which does not restrict the hostname, IP address, or port. An attacker can supply URLs pointing to internal services (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:8080), cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/), or services behind DNS names they control. The request is executed with requests.get and the response is returned to the attacker, enabling data exfiltration or interaction with internal APIs. No additional defenses such as allowlists, DNS resolution checks, or network egress filtering are present, making the SSRF exploit reliable. PoC: GET /preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-app.example.com

 This request will cause the server to fetch AWS metadata and return the JSON credentials in the response body.

The application does not accept any remote user input that influences code execution paths. All database queries are static and there are no dynamic imports, eval, exec, subprocess, or unsafe deserialization. Consequently, there is no remotely exploitable RCE vulnerability. PoC: None

The endpoint is vulnerable to LFI via XML External Entity (XXE) injection. By supplying a crafted XML payload with a DOCTYPE that defines a SYSTEM entity pointing to an arbitrary file, the parser will embed the file content into the <customer> element. The code then returns this value in the JSON response, disclosing the file contents. No validation or disabling of entity resolution is performed, so the attack is feasible remotely. PoC: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/xml" --data-binary '<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><order><customer>&xxe;</customer><item sku="123" qty="1"/></order>' http://<target_host>/orders/import

The import_order function directly parses user‑supplied XML with an lxml parser configured to resolve external entities and load external DTDs. This configuration allows the XML parser to issue arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS (and other protocol) requests when processing external entities. Because the request body is fully under attacker control and no whitelist or validation is applied, an attacker can craft XML that triggers a request to any reachable internal or external service (e.g., cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254, internal APIs, or attacker‑controlled servers). Therefore the application is vulnerable to SSRF via XML External Entity (XXE) injection. PoC: POST /orders/import HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-app.com
Content-Type: application/xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [ <!ENTITY % remote SYSTEM "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"> %remote; ]>
<order><customer>test</customer></order>

The application contains a remote command injection vulnerability. User-controlled input (host) flows unchecked into a shell command executed with subprocess.run and shell=True, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server. This is a classic RCE vector with high exploitability. PoC: curl "http://victim.com/tools/ping?host=127.0.0.1%20&&%20cat%20/etc/passwd"

The /pricing/quote POST endpoint is vulnerable to remote code execution because the user-controlled 'formula' parameter is evaluated using eval with no restrictions, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary Python code on the server. PoC: curl -X POST http://example.com/pricing/quote -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"plan":"basic","seats":1,"formula":"__import__(\'os\').system(\'id\')"}'

The /card endpoint takes 'to' from query string, inserts it directly into a template string that is then rendered with render_template_string. Because the value becomes part of the template source, an attacker can supply Jinja2 syntax (e.g., {{...}} or {%...%}) to execute code on the server. This is a classic server‑side template injection that enables remote code execution. No sanitization is performed, so the vulnerability is fully exploitable. PoC: GET http://example.com/card?to={{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()[40]('id',shell=True).read()}}&occasion=birthday

The application reflects the 'to' URL parameter into the rendered HTML without escaping. The value is concatenated into the Jinja template source, so any HTML or Jinja syntax supplied by an attacker is interpreted verbatim. This results in a reflected Cross‑Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. An attacker can inject a <script> tag or any other markup that will be sent back to the victim's browser and executed. Because the injection occurs before Jinja rendering, classic auto‑escaping does not apply. The vulnerability is exploitable remotely via a crafted HTTP GET request to /card. PoC: GET /card?to=%3Cscript%3Ealert(document.domain)%3C%2Fscript%3E HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.example.com

The validate_pipeline function directly deserializes untrusted request data using yaml.load with yaml.Loader, which is unsafe. An attacker can supply a crafted YAML payload containing !!python/object/apply to execute arbitrary commands on the server, resulting in a remote code execution vulnerability. PoC: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data "!!python/object/apply:os.system ['id']" http://target_host/pipelines/validate

The application does not reflect user-controlled input into an HTML or JavaScript context. It only returns a JSON payload via Flask jsonify, which safely encodes values. Consequently, there is no XSS vulnerability in the provided code. PoC: None

The endpoint allows unauthenticated users to specify any filename ending with .txt or .env within the REPORT_DIR. Because there is no verification that the requester owns or is permitted to view the requested file, an attacker can enumerate or guess filenames (e.g., user123.txt, admin_report.txt, .env) and retrieve their contents. The realpath/commonpath checks only prevent path traversal, not unauthorized file access. Therefore, the 'name' parameter functions as an insecure direct object reference, leading to an IDOR vulnerability. PoC: curl 'http://<host>/reports/download?name=admin.env'   # retrieve .env file if present
curl 'http://<host>/reports/download?name=user123.txt'   # retrieve another user's report

The application does not perform any outbound HTTP/HTTPS or other protocol requests based on user‑supplied URLs. The only user‑controlled input is an IP address validated by the standard library before being used as a direct argument to the ping command, which eliminates command injection risk. As SSRF specifically requires server‑side fetching of remote resources via URLs, this code lacks such a sink, so no SSRF vulnerability is found. PoC: None

The /card endpoint reflects the 'to' query parameter into the HTML response without escaping. Because render_template_string uses a string template, Jinja's auto‑escaping is disabled, so the value is inserted raw into a

element. An attacker can supply a payload such as

to break out of the tag and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. This is a reflected Cross‑Site Scripting vulnerability. PoC: http://vulnerable-site.com/card?to=%3Cscript%3Ealert('XSS')%3C%2Fscript%3E

The provided code does not expose any Local File Inclusion vulnerability. User-controlled data (email) never influences file system paths or template loading paths, and all file operations are internal and static.

The view safely joins the user‑supplied template name with each configured template directory via Django's safe_join, which blocks path traversal. Consequently, an attacker cannot force the server to read files outside those directories, eliminating a remote LFI vector. No other file‑access functions are used. Hence no exploitable LFI is present. PoC: None

The view is reachable via a URL that includes a user‑controlled "template" segment. That value is combined with trusted template directories using Path concatenation, which does not block ".." components. The resulting path is read and its contents returned in the response, allowing remote attackers to read any file readable by the Django process, constituting a remotely exploitable Local File Inclusion vulnerability. PoC: GET /admin/doc/template/../../../../etc/passwd/ HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.example.com

Potential reflected XSS exists if admin_doc/template_detail.html outputs the 'name' variable (the raw URL-supplied template name) without proper HTML escaping. The view does not perform any sanitization, so an attacker can craft a URL containing HTML/JS payload as the template parameter, which will be reflected in the rendered page. Additionally, if the template displays file contents directly ({{ template.contents }}) without escaping, an attacker who can place a malicious file in any of the template directories (e.g., via another upload feature) could achieve stored XSS. Both require confirmation of the template rendering logic. PoC: http://example.com/admin/docs/template_detail/<script>alert(document.domain)</script>/

No remotely exploitable RCE vulnerability detected in the supplied code. The module only validates key format and returns raw bytes; it does not execute code, invoke shell commands, or deserialize untrusted data. Without evidence of user‑controlled data reaching a dangerous sink, the confidence in the absence of RCE is high. PoC: None
